Prism.Core.Contracts uses explicit <Compile Include> links to pull ~20 files out of<br>core/lib/ and core/Services/ into one contract assembly, so records stay next to the code that owns them while<br>every host still depends on one small, dependency-free package. Generate has no separate assembly — it lives in<br>Prism.Core and is a “public service” by deployment, not by compilation." style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#52606D;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="150" y="584" width="1066" height="68" as="geometry"/></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel></diagram></mxfile>
svg.text: 13 projects in jb/src/PRISM.sln. Arrows point at what a project references. Nothing points back up.
services/ — one public service per host
Services/Transform, Services/Upscale, lib/Excel, lib/Ingress, lib/Export, lib/Zip
PipelineFixture — classlib, not a test project
Every test project references Prism.Core and
by the split, so a --filter on PrismCoreTests.<Suite>
still works whichever project a suite lives in.
Physical folder ≠ assembly. Prism.Core.Contracts uses explicit <Compile Include> links to pull ~20 files out of
core/lib/ and core/Services/ into one contract assembly, so records stay next to the code that owns them while
every host still depends on one small, dependency-free package. Generate has no separate assembly — it lives in
Prism.Core and is a “public service” by deployment, not by compilation.
